 World War II is one of the most devastating military conflicts in human history, impacting the world for generations. The enormous cultural event has been the subject of dozens of movies, TV shows, and other media projects. Some stray further into fiction, which deliver an engaging experience but aren't a true representation of the war. A few have been acknowledged by veterans for their accuracy or for capturing the real emotions or experience in wartime.

 The following movies received praise from veterans, including from individuals who were part of the events depicted. Each one also received nominations or awards at the annual Academy Awards, highlighting their impact at the time and their lasting impression on the genre.
 'Fury'
 This World War II Movie Highlights the Loss of Innocence
 What It Is: Fury's star-studded cast takes us on one last ride during the end days of World War II. Logan Lerman joins a grizzled tank crew led by Brad Pitt , and is taken aback by the violence and cruelty of war. The film shows us the loss of innocence in battle, and how people were forced to adapt to survive.
 What Veterans Had to Say About It: World War II tank gunners attended the Fury premiere, seeing some of their real-life exploits on the big screen. While they acknowledged how Hollywood makes things bigger than they seem (via Military Times ), they also explained how the movie was an accurate depiction of their experience as a tank crew.
 Similarly, Bill Betts, a radio operator on a Sherman tank during World War II, discussed the combat accuracy of the film. " Fury accurately portrays how superior the German tanks were, " Betts said in an interview with The Guardian . " A Sherman provided you with protection against most enemy fire but against a Tiger it could easily become your coffin. "

 'The Best Years of Our Lives' (1946)
 The Aftermath of War Is Just as Significant
 A still from the classic war film,  The Best Years of Our Lives RKO Radio Pictures 
 What It Is: The Best Years of Our Lives resonates with veterans not for its depiction of combat or battlefield comradery, but for its relatable narrative of what happens when the fighting stops. The movie follows three World War II veterans as they return home, readjusting to civilian life after their traumatic time in the military.
 Each individual struggles to readjust to society, including dealing with injuries, PTSD flashbacks, and relying on alcohol to cope. The depicted challenges hit close to home for many veterans, who saw their personal experiences on the big screen.

 What Veterans Had to Say About It: General Omar Bradley, a World War II veteran, was impressed by the film, and went as far as arranging for it to be shown to his VA headquarters staff. According to the U.S. Department of Veteran Affairs , he also wrote a letter to the film's producer, Samuel Goldwyn, expressing his appreciation. " I cannot thank you too much for bringing this story to the American public ," Bradley wrote in his note.
 The Best Years of Our Lives won seven Academy Awards, including Best Picture, Best Director, Best Actor, and Best Film Editing, and Russell won the Best Supporting Actor award for his role as Homer Parrish. It was also one of the first 25 films to be selected by the Library of Congress for preservation in the United States National Film Registry for being " culturally, historically, or aesthetically significant. "

 'The Longest Day' (1962)
 One of the Best War Films, According to Veterans
 Close 20th Century Fox 
 20th Century Fox 
 20th Century Fox 
 What It Is: The Longest Day is an ambitious film covering D-Day, the date on which allied forces landed on the beaches of France to invade Europe, and the days leading up to the historic event. The movie shows the preparations and reactions of both sides, including the Americans, the British, Germans, and French.
 The Longest Day's ensemble cast includes John Wayne and Henry Fonda, and the production included several Allied and Axis D-Day participants as consultants. Many of these consultants were directly depicted on screen.
 What Veterans Had to Say About It: Robert L. Williams, a 101st Airborne veteran, describes the movie as one of the best films ever made in an oral history segment for the National World War II Museum . " John Wayne on D-Day was the best movie ever made ," Williams said. " That was fantastic. I remember when the brochure came out, and I have the magazine downstairs. When I saw it, it was great. " He also prefers some of its portrayal over another entry on our list, which he says went a little " too Hollywood " after its opening sequence.
 The Longest Day won Best Cinematography and Best Special Effects at the 35th Academy Awards. It was also nominated for Best Picture and Best Film Editing.

 'Hacksaw Ridge' (2016)
 "I Think He Would Like This Movie."
 What It Is: Hacksaw Ridge isn't a classic war movie in the traditional sense. Desmond Doss, the main character played by Andrew Garfield, refuses to carry a weapon into battle because of religious constraints, but goes on to be awarded the Medal of Honor for his heroic efforts.
 What Veterans Had to Say About It: Carl Levi, a retired brigadier general in the Tennessee Army National Guard who knew Doss for decades, appreciated the film and believed his late friend would've enjoyed the adaption. " I think he would like the movie because it doesn't glorify war. " Levi told the American Legion . " It shows the human side of Desmond — how he saved lives and what he did. He could have picked up a rifle and killed several Japanese, but he didn't. "
 Hacksaw Ridge received six nominations at the 89th Academy Awards, including Best Picture and Best Actor. Ultimately, the film secured the Best Film Editing and Best Sound Mixing awards.

 'Letters From Iwo Jima' (2006)
 The World War II Japanese Perspective Overshadows the Western Companion Piece
 Close Ken Watanabe's General Kuribayashi saluting in Letters from Iwo Jima Warner Bros. Pictures 
 Ken Watanabe as General Kuribayashi in Letters from Iwo Jima Warner Bros. Pictures 
 Kene Watanabe's General Kuribayashi looking on stoically in Letters from Iwo Jima Warner Bros. Pictures 
 What It Is: Letters From Iwo Jima is the companion piece to Flags of Our Fathers , depicting the Battle of Iwo Jima from the perspective of Japanese soldiers. Despite the non-traditional perspective, Letters From Iwo Jima is often considered the superior of the two films, performing better with critics, with a 91% critic score on Rotten Tomatoes , while Flags of Our Fathers sits at just 76% on Rotten Tomatoes . The movie also made more at the box office, with just under $69 million (via Box Office Mojo ), $3 million more than Flags of Our Fathers .
 What Veterans Had to Say About It: In an interview with The Guardian , Kiyoshi Endo, a Japanese Iwo Jima veteran, discussed his confidence in Clint Eastwood's ability to depict his fallen comrades with honor. " I asked him to make a human drama, not a war film, " Endo said. " I wanted him to show how the soldiers felt when they were fighting and, having read the script, I think he has done that. "
 Letters From Iwo Jima won the Best Sound Editing Award at the 79th Academy Awards and was nominated for Best Picture and Best Director.

 'Saving Private Ryan' (1998)
 The Iconic World War II Masterpiece
 What It Is: Saving Private Ryan deserves a spot on any World War II list for the spectacle and brutality captured on screen. The opening sequence depicting the D-Day landing doesn't shy away from the horrors the soldiers faced as they stormed the beach and has served as an inspiration for war movies that followed.
 What Veterans Had to Say About It: Giovanni Ribisi, who played the medic Irwin Wade, took his grandfather Dr. Albert Ribisi to see the Los Angeles premiere. Dr. Ribisi served as a military surgeon during World War II and later served in the Korean War. The movie brought Dr. Ribisi to tears, according to the Los Angeles Times . " We'd never talked about [his service] until the movie ," Ribisi said. " Afterward, I saw this side of him I'd never seen. In the car on the way home from the film he completely opened up. I was blown away. "
 This was not an isolated event. World War II paratrooper Jack Evans saw the film at a special early screening for veterans, and stated that the depicted violence was gruesome, but was realistic (via Times Leader ).
 The second part of the movie leans into Hollywood fantasy, with a heroic journey and last stand against a battalion, but the film does enough for most to overlook this departure from reality and cement itself as one of the greatest war movies of all time. Saving Private Ryan won multiple awards, including Best Director and Best Cinematography at the 71st Academy Awards. Tom Hanks was also nominated for Best Actor.
